Thanks for the context. A few operational notes before decisioning:

- We need clarity on whether the 0.25% refresh is additive to her standard grant or a replacement. If additive, we need sign‑off from comp council and cap table impact review.
- For cash sign‑on: we typically cap one‑time payments at $25k for this band unless there is Sr‑level justification. If Soojin can confirm business impact (quantify revenue or strategic risk) I can route for expedited approval.
- Please attach the candidate's targeted start date and confirm whether she will be eligible for relocation (her note: "no relocation needed").

I'll prepare two approval paths: (A) $25k cash + 0.25% refresh (additive) submitted to comp council for expedited review, or (B) $35k cash (no refresh) approved as an ad‑hoc exception if comp council declines extra equity.

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Talent Partner, Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Olivia Grant - verbal acceptance threshold / competing offer

Appreciate the urgency. My position: we should prefer equity where possible to preserve cash and long‑term alignment. Approve path A with the following constraints:

- Cash make‑whole capped at $20k (gross) to be paid on first payroll.
- Equity refresh of 0.20% (slightly below requested) as an additive grant; vesting synced to the existing schedule, cliff waived per standard refresh rules.
- Exception approval will be conditional on a short business memo from Soojin quantifying the "revenue at risk" or clear KPIs Olivia will own; this memo will be stored with the approval ticket.

If Soojin cannot produce the memo within 24 hours, we hold the refresh and approve up to $30k cash as an alternative (no equity).

Markus Klein
Director, Compensation & Benefits
